title: Beyond Basic A/B Testing: Improving Statistical Efficiency for Business Growth

problem.claim: Standard A/B testing approaches based mostly on t-tests have low statistical power in business settings involving small samples, non-Gaussian distributions, ROI considerations, or confounding.

gap.claim: A single framework is needed to address small samples, distribution robustness, ROI, and confounding while allowing flexible treatment-effect definitions.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes the statistical efficiency of estimating equations and U statistics for addressing the identified testing issues.
The paper proposes a doubly robust generalized U framework with flexible treatment-effect definitions and simultaneous handling of small samples, distribution robustness, ROI, and confounding.
The paper provides theoretical results on asymptotics and efficiency bounds, including insights into efficiency gains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the doubly robust generalized U as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive simulation studies.
The authors report applying the methods to multiple real A/B tests at LinkedIn.
The authors report sharing broadly useful results and learnings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Industry A/B testing commonly relies on t-test-based approaches.
These approaches can have low statistical power under business-relevant data and objective conditions.
The paper studies estimating equations and U statistics and proposes a doubly robust generalized U framework.
The paper derives asymptotic and efficiency-bound results and analyzes efficiency gains.
The methods are evaluated through simulations and multiple real LinkedIn A/B tests.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative effect sizes, power gains, or efficiency values.
The abstract does not specify the datasets, simulation settings, comparator methods, or detailed assumptions.
The abstract does not provide implementation, reproducibility, or full-text details.
